mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows the model to invent access attempts where a clinician who is NOT on the care team can still have a Permitted outcome. This directly violates the care-team-membership gating rule, which is the core authorization invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CareTeamGateBreach { some attempt: AccessAttempt, member: CareTeamMembership | attempt.actor.role in (Doctor + Nurse + Pharmacist + ClinicalAdmin) and attempt.outcome = Permitted and not (member.clinician = attempt.actor and member.patient = attempt.target_patient and member.status = Active) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact breaks the one-to-one correspondence between access attempts and audit entries, and allows audit entries to be disconnected from the attempts they record. This violates both the completeness and attribution correctness invariants.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditMismatch { some audit1, audit2: AuditEntry | audit1 != audit2 and audit1.recorded_actor = audit2.recorded_actor and audit1.access_attempt.actor != audit2.access_attempt.actor }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows audit entries to have inconsistent authorisation basis (e.g., Permitted outcome with NotCareTeamMember basis, which is logically impossible). This violates the audit entry shape constraint.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthBasisInconsistency { some audit: AuditEntry | audit.outcome = Permitted and audit.authorisation_basis != CareTeamMember }

mutation_targets.rationale: When the universe is empty, universally quantified predicates like 'all audit: AuditEntry | ...' become vacuously true. Removing this fact causes assertions to pass trivially without constraining anything meaningful. This is a test of predicate non-vacuity.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PopulateUniverse { some User; some Patient; some CareTeamMembership; some AccessAttempt; some AuditEntry }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the permission matrix facts allows the model to invent arbitrary role-operation pairs, violating the least-privilege principle. Specifically, clinical roles could gain access to SearchAuditLog or AuditOfficer could gain access to LookupPatientRecord.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermissionBreach { some role: (Doctor + Nurse + Pharmacist + ClinicalAdmin) | role -> SearchAuditLog in PermissionMatrix.allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows the model to invent outcomes outside the defined set, violating the closed-world assumption on access outcomes and making it impossible to ensure all paths are audited with valid outcomes.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_InvalidOutcome { some audit: AuditEntry | audit.outcome not in (Permitted + Denied + NotFoundOrDenied) }
